description: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab, carboplatin and paclitaxel is recommended, within its marketing authorisation, as an option for treating metastatic non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults who have not had treatment for their metastatic NSCLC before and whose PD-L1 tumour proportion score is between 0% and 49% (with no EGFR- or ALK-positive mutations), or when targeted therapy for EGFR-positive or ALK-positive NSCLC has failed. It is recommended only if: it is stopped at 2 years of uninterrupted treatment, or earlier as specified, and the company provides atezolizumab and bevacizumab according to the commercial arrangements.

extensions.name: statement description
extensions.value: The U.K. National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) has recommended atezolizumab, within its marketing authorisation, plus bevacizumab, carboplatin and paclitaxel as an option for treating metastatic non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer in adults who have not had treatment for their metastatic NSCLC before and whose PD-L1 tumour proportion score is between 0% and 49% (no EGFR- or ALK-positive mutations), or when targeted therapy for EGFR-positive or ALK-positive NSCLC has failed. Treatment is stopped at 2 years of uninterrupted treatment, or earlier if there is loss of clinical benefit (atezolizumab) or disease progression (bevacizumab). Atezolizumab and bevacizumab are recommended within their marketing authorisation and subject to the commercial arrangements available to the NHS.
